name: Global temperature
summary: Global temperature 1.85°C above pre-industrial on 7 Nov, a record for the date
state: ERA5 data for 7 Nov put global surface air temperature at 14.62°C, about 1.85°C above pre-industrial levels and a record for the calendar date, above the 1.6°C Alert line (Climate Reanalyzer). The estimate adds 0.88°C to the 1991–2020 anomaly of 0.97°C. Readings have eased from about 2.05°C in early November but every day since late October has stayed above 1.8°C, with the very strong El Niño adding heat.
for_you: Record global heat raises the odds of heatwaves, heavy rain and marine heatwaves in many regions. National met services publish warnings for local extremes.
rubric_hit: Alert: +1.85°C > +1.6°C and a record high for the calendar date (7 Nov)

sources.title: Climate Reanalyzer — Daily global surface air temperature (ERA5)

why: Global temperature is the master climate variable; each tenth of a degree raises extreme-weather risk.
drivers: Greenhouse gases, El Niño/La Niña, aerosols, solar cycle.

rubric.alert: > +1.6°C, or a record high for the calendar date.
rubric.normal: Daily global anomaly < +1.3°C above pre-industrial (ERA5 vs 1991–2020 + 0.88°C).
